text: Titan was different. Its middle was a tube of carbon fibre, about thirteen centimetres thick, built up from layers of fibre and glue. At each end, a titanium dome, joined to the tube by titanium rings, glued in place. A tube holds more people than a sphere. And carbon fibre is light, and incredibly strong when you pull on it. But deep underwater, a hull isn't pulled. It's squeezed. And for thick carbon fibre under squeezing, again and again, there's far less proof. Its layers can start to separate, and the damage hides inside. And carbon fibre and titanium squeeze by different amounts, which loads the joints between them. It was a new kind of hull, taking people this deep, and it was never certified by an outside inspector.
